title: Medjugorje Bread
directions: Mix well, spread in two bread pans about two inches thick. Bake at 400 deg. for 30 to 45 minutes. Remember this bread will not rise.
Instead of yogurt, you can use 1 1/2 to 2 cups of milk. - Add 3/4 cups of sunflower seeds for even more flavor.
Enjoy, and good fasting.

title: Potato Dinner Rolls
ingredients: 1/2 cup water or reserved potato water (125 mL)
directions: Over medium heat melt butter. Add potato water and milk, heat just to lukewarm, set aside.
Put mashed potatoes and potato water mixture in a large bowl. Add the sugar, salt and eggs. Beat with a wire whisk until smooth. Add Fermipan yeast over mixture and beat again.

Add 2 cups (500 mL) of flour, beat until smooth. Mix in 3 1/2 more cups (875 mL) of flour with a wooden spoon. Gradually add the last cup (250 mL) of flour, working it in with your hands by pressing flour into dough and turning dough over, until you have a firm dough.
Cover and let rise in the same bowl for 40 minutes, or until double in bulk.

Punch dough down, place on floured surface. Sprinkle dough lightly with flour. Press dough out with fingers to a square 1 inch (2.5 cm) thick. Cut in strips lengthwise 1 1/2" (4 cm) and crosswise 1 1/2" (4 cm). Then you have 1 1/2" (4 cm) squares. If knife gets sticky when cutting just dust with flour.
Shape each square into a ball by pinching all four sides underneath to seal. Place buns almost touching in greased round or square cake pans.
Let rise covered for one hour or until doubled.
Bake in a preheated 400° F (200° C) oven for 15-20 minutes. For a soft crust brush tops with margarine or butter. Cool on racks. Makes about 40.
notes: Printed clipping (the 'Co-op paper' source of the handwritten card in photos 182-183)
Intro: 'These are wonderful, old fashioned rolls. Don't expect any left for the next day.'

Put mashed potatoes and potato water mixture in a large bowl. Add the sugar, salt and eggs. Beat with a wire whisk until smooth. Add Fermipan yeast over mixture and beat again.
Add 2 cups (500 mL) of flour, beat until smooth. Mix in 3 1/2 more cups (875 mL) of flour with a wooden spoon. Gradually add the last cup (250 mL) of flour, working it in with your hands by pressing flour into dough and turning dough over, until you have a firm dough.
Cover and let rise in the same bowl for 40 minutes, or until double in bulk.
Punch dough down, place on floured surface. Sprinkle dough lightly with flour. Press dough out with fingers to a square 1 inch (2.5 cm) thick. Cut in strips lengthwise 1 1/2" (4 cm) and crosswise 1 1/2" (4 cm). Then you have 1 1/2" (4 cm) squares. If knife gets sticky when cutting just dust with flour.
Shape each square into a ball by pinching all four sides underneath to seal. Place buns almost touching in greased round or square cake pans.
Let rise covered for one hour or until doubled.
Bake in a preheated 400° F (200° C) oven for 15-20 minutes. For a soft crust brush tops with margarine or butter. Cool on racks. Makes about 40.
